chapter: Chicago, Ohio and Jelly Roll Morton
title: Playing Jelly's stop-chorus dance arrangements; Tommy Benford
summary: He describes the chorus-by-chorus modulating dance format, Jelly's out-of-state status, and Tommy Benford on drums.

bands.name: Jelly Roll Morton's Red Hot Peppers

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Remembering Jelly Roll Morton: the man, the band

blocks.x: Yeah. See, he was playing one of them dance halls where you play one chorus, and then when into another chorus, and went into another chorus. And there's one advantage that Jelly had. By him being an out-of-state musician, it didn't make no difference if he brought another guy from out of town. He could get a musician anywhere in the world he wanted, any place in the United States to join his band, because he already had made it traveling himself. Because he didn't belong in 802. So they accepted me. Because I didn't make no mistakes. All I had to do was learn what they did. And they'd play one chorus, stop, and then play another chorus, stop, and then make a modulation and go to another chorus, stop, then play the chorus. So that was nothing to me. And then later on, he recorded the Hot Peppers in New York, and...
Do you remember any of those other guys? Do you remember who the rhythm section was? Was it the Benford Brothers...?
Tommy Benford was on drums. Was his brother playing bass?
I think so, yeah. Because Tommy Benford told some guy overseas about me. He wrote me, but I didn't give no information. I just didn't feel... See, after I heard
about Jelly was so big, I didn't give out none of the knowledge I knew about him. Because I liked him, you know. He was...
